reaction.episode: CORRECTION through the Nov 24 close (data fresh, not stale): SPX 7,201.09, down 8.2% from its 120-day high, 5.4% below its 50-day and 2.0% below its 200-day; SMH $426.75 and NVDA $155.38 both BELOW Zone 2 (SMH Zone 2 $470-505, NVDA Zone 2 $175-185), down 36.5% and 36.2% from their highs; VIX 26.36 after spiking to a 5-day high of 35.89 (rollover signal confirmed); HY OAS 3.63, calm; mechanical capitulation tally 2 of 4 (VIX rollover and credit calm confirmed, zone occupancy and volume climax not).
reaction.invalidation: The Watch stance is wrong if SPX reclaims 7,300 on a weekly close AND VIX closes under 25 — the two remaining legs of the standing thesis falsifier (the NVDA leg is already met at $155.38, above $150) — or if a confirmed bottom forms (a failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds, with the 10-year falling). Either voids this ladder and flips the posture to staged adding.

ladder.response: Treat as the correction deepening toward a regime break: no new entries of any kind, keep new money in bills, re-audit the next zone down before acting.
ladder.trigger: Escalation: SPX closes below 7,000, or SMH closes below $400

ladder.response: Do not chase the bounce and do not treat it as re-entry. A failed bounce into the failure zone is the trap verdict — no adds; trim leveraged beta (TQQQ/CONL) only on that confirmed strength, never into weakness.
ladder.trigger: Trap: SMH bounces into the failure zone $580-600 (SPX $7,750-7,820) and fails there with a lower high

ladder.response: Stand-down in force: all buying halted, the deployment ladder suspended, and the thesis re-audited from scratch — the rotation read is dead and the regime-break call takes over.
ladder.trigger: Stand-down: HY OAS closes above 4.00%, or VIX closes above 35 again with SPX below 7,000

ladder.response: Probe-sized entries per the deployment ladder (Tranche A conditions met): start with the highest-conviction DATA_AHEAD names (PLTR, ONTO, AVGO) in small size, scaling only if the reclaim holds for a second close.
ladder.trigger: Re-entry: SMH reclaims Zone 2 ($470-505) with NVDA back into $175-185 AND the mechanical tally reaches 3 of 4

reaction.trapRisk: The tape is already showing the trap shape: NVDA fell 5.86% and SMH 7.26% on Nov 24 while both sit below Zone 2, so any sharp bounce from here into the failure zone (SMH $580-600, SPX $7,750-7,820) that fails there is a bull trap, not a bottom. Entries must wait for the failure-zone retest verdict and a second low that holds — no chasing the first green day, and no sizing up on a single-day reversal while the tally sits at 2 of 4.

strategyPosture: Watch. The episode is a CORRECTION, not a confirmed regime break, but no bottom is confirmed either: SMH and NVDA sit below Zone 2, the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4, and credit calm is the one leg holding the rotation read together. No new buying into a falling tape, and no selling into panic after an 8.2% SPX drawdown — the work now is watching the zone reclaim and the credit tripwire.

themes.counterRead: The index is not the market, and the divergence is the signal: a 12-point Mag7-vs-SPX gap means the correction is a leadership unwind, not broad selling. But the read is rotation, not rollover — bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.63% and calm — so the concentration theme says 'watch the gap,' not 'the market is broken.' If credit flips, rotation becomes rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: The damage is concentrated in the names that dominate index weight. The Mag7 average sits 20.09% below its 52-week highs against SPY's 8%, a 12.09-point gap; NVDA is the weakest at 36.2% below its high while AAPL is the strongest at just 1.9% below. QQQ is down 12.87% over one month against SPY's 7.82%, and SMH carries a 36.48% drawdown from its high. Breadth is thin: the only one-month leader in the whole universe is TMDX (+32.27%), a healthcare name still 40.1% below its high, and MA (+5.17%) is the only other gainer.
themes.label: Index Calm Masks a Concentrated Unwind
themes.narrative: The index tape reads as an orderly correction: SPX closed Nov 24 at 7,201.09, down just 0.5% on the day and 8.2% from its 120-day high, and this morning's pre-market snapshot shows SPY at 705.5, down 2.32%. The story is 'a normal pullback.'
themes.watchFor: Mag7-vs-SPX gap widening past 15 points, or SLOOS rising toward the 40% stress threshold.

themes.counterRead: This is the clearest DATA_AHEAD setup in the tape — fundamentals and price moving in opposite directions — but it is unconfirmed. The mechanical tally is only 2 of 4: zone occupancy and volume-climax signals are NOT confirmed, and SMH ($426.75) and NVDA ($155.38) sit BELOW Zone 2 rather than in it. A derating can overshoot further, and AVGO reports Dec 9 after the close — a miss reprices the 'recovery confirmed' read. The setup is real; the entry is not yet earned.
themes.dataAnchor: The fundamentals have not followed the price. NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY while the stock sits 36.2% below its high; AVGO is growing 55% YoY at 39.2% below its high; LRCX is growing 131.3% YoY at 55.3% below its high; ONTO is growing 41.5% YoY at 55.1% below its high; PLTR is growing 91.7% YoY at 24.3% below its high. Insiders are buying the trough: PLTR saw $122.25M of insider buying, ROK $1.55M, ETN $0.32M, KTOS $0.2M. Conviction scores run 78-90 (PLTR 90, ETN 88, ONTO 85, AVGO 83).
themes.label: AI Supply Chain: Revenues Growing, Multiples Collapsing
themes.narrative: The AI trade is broken. Semis and AI software are being sold as if demand has gone: NVDA fell 10.77% in this morning's snapshot and SMH fell 7.26% on Nov 24 alone, with the whole complex 24-56% below its highs.
themes.watchFor: SMH reclaiming Zone 2 ($470-505) with NVDA back into $175-185 and the mechanical tally reaching 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: The selloff is sentiment, not a power-demand break — but that cuts both ways. These names trade with the AI complex, not on their own fundamentals, so they need AI capex confirmation, not more power headlines, to bottom. VST's flat revenue inflection means this is a repricing of AI capex expectations, not a mispriced power thesis. No bottom call until the semis complex stabilizes.
themes.dataAnchor: VST sits 33.9% below its high at $120.72 and VRT 54.3% below at $173.82, with GEV down 18.86% and URA down 22.35% over one month. The dislocation data labels both VST's and VRT's declines SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental, and the opportunity signals still flag the structural demand theme as active for the group. But VST's own revenue inflection is STABLE_OR_DECLINING, not recovering — the holding is a power supplier whose growth has flattened.
themes.label: AI Power: The Demand Story Has Not Broken, the Price Has
themes.narrative: Nuclear and AI-power names are collapsing with the AI complex: VST down 17.51% in a month, VRT down 17.91%, OKLO down 28.84%, SMR down 39.85%, CCJ down 26.61%. The story reads as if the power buildout is being cancelled.
themes.watchFor: SMH reclaiming Zone 2 ($470-505) — the power names bottom with the AI complex, not before it.

themes.counterRead: The washout tells us nothing about the next leg — it is mechanical deleveraging, not new information. There is no bottom signal in the data, and the standing add condition for BMNR (an ETH reclaim) is nowhere near met on a 31.9% down month. The correct read is that leverage did its job in both directions; the portfolio question is sizing, not timing a crypto bottom.
themes.dataAnchor: The drawdowns scale exactly with leverage, which is what the instruments are designed to do. CONL fell 15.81% in this morning's snapshot and 63.3% over one month against BTC's 26.9%; TQQQ fell 13.73% on the day and 38.1% over the month against QQQ's 12.87%; BMNR fell 10.61% on the day and 38.47% over the month; DOGE fell 30.35% over the month; COIN fell 37.02%. All four leveraged/crypto holdings sit in the one-month laggards list, and there is no fundamental anchor in the data for any of them.
themes.label: Leveraged Crypto: The Washout Is Mechanical
themes.narrative: Crypto is crashing: BTC down 26.9% in a month, ETH down 31.9%, and the leveraged holdings are being wiped out — CONL down 63.3% in a month, TQQQ down 38.1%, BMNR down 38.5%.
themes.watchFor: BTC-USD one-month performance back above -10%, or CONL/TQQQ daily declines slowing below 5% on a down day.

themes.counterRead: This is the single most important divergence in the tape. Credit calm is what separates a correction from a credit event, and it is the leg that keeps the rotation read alive. If HY OAS closes above 4.00%, the rotation read dies and the regime-break call takes over — that line is the tripwire, and it is 37bp away. Until then, the equity panic is running ahead of what credit actually shows.
themes.dataAnchor: Credit is not confirming any of it. HY OAS is 3.63%, flagged calm and not cracking, 37 basis points below the 4.00% stand-down line. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7%. The curve has un-inverted (2s10s +0.29) with the 10-year at 4.92%, the real 10-year at 2.8%, and the fed funds rate at 3.88%. The bond market is pricing an orderly correction; the equity tape is pricing distress.
themes.label: Credit Is Not Confirming the Panic
themes.narrative: Fed fears are driving the tape: PCE inflation data lands today (Nov 25), the FOMC minutes event is active with HIGH signal strength, the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision and Dec 10 CPI both carry HIGH signal strength, and headlines warn of worsening AI-stock volatility ahead of the inflation prints.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS daily close above 4.00%, or the Oct PCE print today materially surprising to the hawkish side.

watchFor: SPX weekly close vs 7,300 (thesis falsifier leg) and vs 7,000 (regime-break line)
SMH/NVDA reclaim of Zone 2 ($470-505 / $175-185) vs a close below SMH $400
VIX close under 25 (falsifier leg) vs a renewed spike above 35
Oct PCE print today Nov 25, Dec 8-9 FOMC decision, and AVGO earnings Dec 9 after the close
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI supply chain, and it breaks one of two ways: a confirmed bottom forms when SMH and NVDA reclaim Zone 2 with the tally reaching 3 of 4, or the correction deepens toward the next zone down (SMH below $400, SPX below 7,000). Today's PCE print and the Dec 8-9 FOMC decision are the catalysts that decide which.
